'Twenty-fifth of March, 1891.' counts as 4 words but is spoken as about 7 ('eighteen ninety-one'). The hard checks said 'All passed'.
issues.proposed_change: Add `spoken_words(text)`, which expands each 4-digit year to 3 words, other numbers to their spoken length, and '£250' to 4. For each line, compute est_end = t_start + spoken_words/2.5. Flag the line if est_end > next line's t_start - 0.2, or if est_end > seg.duration_s - 1.0 on the last segment ('leave the last second for picture'). Use spoken_words in word_budget too. Also flag the first line if t_start < 0.8 in segment 1.

issues.problem: Nothing in code checks the renderability rules the prompt asks for. Two camera moves in one shot, too many settings in one 15 s generation, faces in shots that have narration, very short shots, and unused or over-referenced assets all pass silently.
issues.evidence: Final segment 1 shot 3 camera is 'Slow drift alongside, then gentle tilt up'. The second review flagged it, but the loop stopped on pass. Segment 2 packs 4 shots across 3 settings (aerial harbour, sand close-up, hall crane, jaw close-up) in 15 s, with the shortest shot 3.5 s. Segment 2 shot 3 contains 'visitors' faces'.
issues.proposed_change: Add these checks. (1) MULTI = re.compile(r'\b(then|and then|before|followed by|as it|while)\b', re.I) on shot.camera, plus a count of motion verbs in shot.action: flag 'shot N has more than one camera move or action'. (2) shot length < 2.5 s → flag. (3) more than 2 distinct shot.setting values per segment → flag 'too many locations for one generation'. (4) re.search(r'\b(face|faces|mouth|lips|speaking|talking)\b') in visual/action while narration exists → flag 'face in frame will attract lip-synced narration'. (5) every asset used by at least one segment; every shot.refs is a subset of seg.ref_assets; len(seg.ref_assets) <= 4. (6) duration must be a whole second between 4 and 15 (fal enum).

issues.problem: The S3 prompt gives no Seedance-specific craft guidance. It does not say how reference images work, what to avoid (faces, repeating fine structures, multi-move cameras, many locations), how to compose for a phone, or how to keep the subject identical across shots. The script that comes out is a nice storyboard with several shots that are likely to morph.
issues.evidence: Segment 1 shot 2 is a forward dolly under 'rows of ribs… slide past overhead one after another'. Fast-moving repeated thin structures shimmer, merge or change in count in current video models. Segment 1 shot 1 asks for an 'endless chain of vertebrae', which invites the model to make the skeleton longer. Segment 1 holds both the skeleton and living_whale references, and with no per-shot binding the model can blend them (a skeleton swimming, or a whale with visible ribs).
issues.proposed_change: Add a section: 'Writing for Seedance. Each segment becomes one prompt with up to 4 reference images, tagged @Image1… in the order of ref_assets. In each shot, name which image it uses ("the skeleton from @Image1") and never show two reference subjects in the same shot. Keep a segment to at most two settings and at most one jump between them; 3 shots per 15 s is the sweet spot, and each shot runs at least 3 s. One camera move per shot from this list: static, slow push-in, slow pull-back, tilt up/down, crane up/down, slow orbit, tracking alongside. Never chain moves with "then". Avoid what these models get wrong: human faces close-up (and any face while narration plays), hands, fast motion across fine repeating structures (ribs, railings), the subject changing scale or length, objects transforming into other objects, any text. Prefer slow, heavy motion: light moving across a still object, water moving around a still body, the camera moving past a still subject. Paste subject_lock verbatim wherever the exhibit appears, and do not add other adjectives to it. Compose for the stated aspect ratio: in 9:16, show long objects by tilting along them, not in a single wide frame. End each segment on a simple, mostly static image the next segment can cut from.'

issues.problem: The asset (reference image) instructions produce references with scene composition and lighting baked in. With references, the model copies lighting and framing, so mood belongs in the video prompt. The prompt also tells the writer to build every asset from the visitor's photo even when there isn't one.
issues.evidence: `living_whale` prompt: 'noticeably small in the frame', so the subject is tiny in its own reference. `jaw_closeup` has stained-glass 'patches of red, blue and amber light' baked into the bone. `skeleton_full` includes visitors and the hall. All four start with 'Clean reference image based on the visitor's photo' in a run with no photo.
issues.proposed_change: Replace the Reference images paragraph with: 'Reference images. List the references the shots need, at most 4 per segment. Subject references show the exhibit alone, filling the frame, sharp, under even neutral light on a plain background, from one stated view (front, side, three-quarter from below, detail). No mood lighting, no people, no scale tricks. Put lighting, scale and composition in the shot, not in the reference. If one setting appears in several shots, it may get its own environment reference (the empty hall, the empty sandbar). A living or historical form of the exhibit gets its own subject reference, consistent with subject_lock. Set source to visitor_photo only when a photo was provided. Otherwise use museum_photo if the pack has one, or text_only, and write the prompt accordingly.'

issues.problem: The reviewer scores visual_feasibility with generic judgement and no video-model checklist. It can pass a script while still listing fixes, and it never checks whether the previous round's fixes were applied. The result is that known renderability defects reach the final script.
issues.evidence: 06_s4_review returned verdict 'pass' with 4 issues, including 'segment 1 shot 3 asks for two motions… risks an unstable or morphing whale'. run.py breaks on pass, so the fix was never applied, and the final script still has 'Slow drift alongside, then gentle tilt up'. The reviewer also accepted living_whale (underwater) as the reference for the stranded-on-sand shot ('consistent enough', 06 thinking.md). CHANGELOG lists the pass-with-fixes problem as known.
issues.proposed_change: Add this to the visual_feasibility criterion: 'Check each shot against these questions. Is there exactly one camera move and one action? Does the shot's reference image actually show the subject in the state the shot needs (swimming vs stranded vs skeleton)? Are there two reference subjects in one shot? Are there faces, hands, fast motion over repeating structures, scale change or transformation? Are there more than two settings in the segment? Does each segment end on an image the next can cut from? Is there anything that needs a voice to come from a visible person? Any one of these caps visual_feasibility at 3.' Replace the verdict rule with: 'Mark each issue blocking or minor. Verdict is pass only if truth is 5, no score is below 4, and there are no blocking issues. A renderability defect is always blocking. If you list a fix you expect to be applied, the verdict is revise.' Add an `severity: Literal['blocking','minor']` field to Issue in schemas.py.

issues.problem: The report shows the structured script but never the actual Seedance request. Nobody (human or reviewer) can judge whether the prompt is renderable, how the @Image tags line up, or how long it is. METHOD says the agent's output and the Seedance template are kept separate, but the harness has no template, so that separation can't be tested.
issues.evidence: report.md has shot tables and asset prompts but no rendered prompt or fal payload. METHOD §4 says the template is rendered later, and §7 says Seedance prompt syntax is unknown.
issues.proposed_change:
Add a render_seedance(script, seg_index) function that returns {prompt, image_urls order, duration, aspect_ratio, generate_audio}. Format: '@Image1 is <asset view>. @Image2 is …
[Shot 1, 0–5 s] <framing>, <camera>. <action>. <visual>.
Cut to [Shot 2, 5–9.5 s] …
Sound: <ambience>; <sfx>. No speech, no voices, no music. No text or lettering anywhere in frame.' Print one fenced block per segment under '## Seedance requests' in report.md, and pass the rendered prompts to S4 inside <seedance_prompts> so it reviews what will actually be sent.

issues.problem: Fact ids are attached to lines that don't state the fact, and visual-only notes from the pack slip into narration. Code can't catch this, and neither the S3 nor the S4 prompt makes it a rule.
issues.evidence: 'Out there, I was blue, not bone.' is tagged [juvenile_female]. 'Look up. I'm still diving.' rests on the pack's 'Pose (UNSOURCED)' / 'Appearance (for visuals, not narration)', and the reviewer waved it through. A line that states no fact has empty fact_ids; do not attach a nearby fact to make it look sourced. Appearance and pose notes are for pictures only: never state them in narration.' Add this to s4_review truth: 'Check each fact_id against its line: a tag on a line that does not state that fact is an issue. Narration that states anything taken from appearance or UNSOURCED notes scores truth 1.'

issues.problem: S2 hooks and endings are written with no renderability limits, so concepts that can't be rendered reach S3. Only luck kept them out of the final.

issues.proposed_change: Add: 'Every hook and ending must be a picture a video model can make in one shot: a real place or object, one slow motion, no text or numbers on screen, no morphing or dissolving of one object into another, no close-up human faces. Numbers and names are spoken, never shown.'

issues.problem: How the two 15 s segments join is left vague ('end segment 1 on an image segment 2 can pick up from'). The fal reference-to-video endpoint has no first- or last-frame input, so a continuous camera move across the cut will not line up.
issues.evidence: In the final script, segment 1 ends on 'the brightening surface' and segment 2 opens on an aerial 'from pale grey sky'. This works by luck as a brightness match cut; it was never designed that way, and no field records it.

Design the cut: end segment 1 on a near-static image (a bright surface, a dark silhouette, a still close-up) and open segment 2 on an image with matching brightness or shape. Write both in end_frame. Segment 2 reuses at least one of segment 1's subject references so the exhibit looks the same on both sides of the cut.' Optionally, extract segment 1's last frame and pass it to segment 2 as an extra @Image.

issues.problem: The narration rules don't make the writer spell out numbers the way they will be spoken, or keep punctuation that TTS and subtitles handle consistently. Word counts and pacing come out wrong for dates and money.

Round only in a way the fact still supports ("over twenty-five metres" for 25.2). Use full stops and commas, not dashes.' Subtitles can show numerals.

issues.problem: The word budget in code is looser than the one in METHOD and the prompt, so the hard check passes scripts the method would reject.

best_things_to_keep: Pipeline stages S0–S4 with archived request, thinking and output files and hash caching. This run's forensics (finding the dropped asset and the from-scratch rewrite) were only possible because of it.
Separating the agent's judgement (a structured Script) from the Seedance prompt wording (a template). Keep it, and add the renderer so the template exists and can be tested.
One segment = one ≤15 s generation, and a 30 s film = exactly two segments, enforced by checks.
A canonical subject phrase repeated in every shot ('Hope, the pale ivory-cream blue whale skeleton…'). Make it a schema field (subject_lock) rather than relying on habit.
'No text or signage' in every asset prompt, and the TEXT_ON_SCREEN check.

Most shots are already single, slow, heavy motions that suit Seedance: an upward tilt from the hall floor, tide water washing round a still flank, coloured light sliding over still bone. Keep this 'still subject, moving light/water/camera' pattern as the house style.
One world-jump per segment (hall to sea, harbour to hall), and the brightness match at the segment cut (bright water surface to grey sky).
The S1 rule that keeps UNSOURCED and appearance notes out of the fact list, and the fact-id-per-line structure.
S4's concrete fixes (rewritten lines, replacement shot descriptions). The first review's fixes were specific and mostly good; the failures were in the loop plumbing, not in how the reviewer writes.
The narration density in the final script (54 words / 30 s overall) and the short spoken sentences. The line-level timing just needs checking.
The S2 three-concept structure and the choice reasoning from the visitor's point of view. 'Not Even Grown' is a strong, single-turn idea that can be shot.

issues.problem: The revise pass never shows the writer its own draft. s3_script() sends only material, concept and feedback, so S3 attempt 1 writes a whole new script from the review notes. The notes point at lines by timestamp ('segment 1 narration line 3 (6.4s, ...)') that the writer cannot see. That makes the revise loop non-local: things that already worked can change silently, and 'fixed' means 'rewritten'.
issues.evidence: 05_s3_script/thinking.md opens: 'I'm rebuilding the full script from scratch since the original isn't available'. agent.py s3_script() builds user content with no previous script. Between 03 and 05, every shot's action and visual text was rewritten, not only the lines the review named.
issues.proposed_change: Add `previous: schemas.Script | None = None` to agent.s3_script and pass `script` from the previous attempt in run.py. When it is set, append `<previous_script>\n{previous.model_dump_json(indent=2)}\n</previous_script>` before <review_feedback>. Replace the last paragraph of prompts/s3_script.md with: "If a previous script and review feedback are attached, edit the previous script; do not rewrite it. Change only the lines, shots, assets and subtitles the feedback names, plus whatever those changes force (timings, subtitles). Copy everything else exactly. If you decide not to apply a point, because it would add a fact outside the concept or break a rule above, leave that part unchanged and explain why in revision_notes." Add `revision_notes: list[str]` to schemas.Script (empty on the first attempt).

issues.problem: The loop trusts the model's own verdict field. A 'pass' that still lists fixes ends the loop with those fixes unapplied. The schema also asks for scores and verdict BEFORE issues, so the reviewer commits to a verdict before it writes its criticism. Round 2 then landed exactly on the pass threshold (all 4s, truth 5) while it listed 4 issues, one of them a feasibility risk ('risks an unstable or morphing whale').
issues.evidence: 06_s4_review/thinking.md: 'I'm settling on a verdict of pass with minor issues, rating the hook, focus, visuals and ending each a 4'. In report.md, the final S4 has verdict pass plus 4 issues, and the final script still has the two-motion underwater shot the reviewer flagged. run.py line 65: `if review.verdict == "pass" and not problems: break`.
issues.proposed_change: schemas.py: give Issue `severity: Literal["blocking", "polish"]` and reorder Review to `issues`, `scores`, `summary`. Drop `verdict` from what the model writes. run.py: compute `blocking = [i for i in review.issues if i.severity == "blocking"]` and `passed = not problems and not blocking and review.scores.truth == 5 and min(review.scores.model_dump().values()) >= 4`. Stop only when `passed and not review.issues`. If only polish issues remain and attempts are left, send them as feedback once more. s4_review.md: replace the Verdict paragraph with "List every problem first. Mark it blocking if it breaks a fact rule, an automatic check, or is likely to make the video model fail (morphing, two actions, on-screen text, a line that cannot fit its time); otherwise polish. Then score. Scores must agree with the issues: any blocking issue in a dimension caps that dimension at 3." Apply the same order fix to ConceptSet: put choice_reason before chosen.

issues.problem: The loop ships the LAST attempt, not the best one. Nothing marks a script that is still failing after MAX_REVISIONS, although METHOD.md section 2 S4 says to flag it for a human. The report says 'All passed on the final script' even when reviewer issues are still open.
issues.evidence: run.py lines 57-70 write `script` from whichever iteration ran last. render() prints 'All passed on the final script.' under Hard checks, while the S4 section of this run lists 4 unapplied fixes.
issues.proposed_change: Keep a list of (script, review, problems) per attempt and pick `best = min(attempts, key=lambda a: (len(a.problems), len(blocking(a.review)), -a.review.scores.truth, -min(scores)))`. Write a top-line `status` into report.md and script.json: PASS, PASS_WITH_OPEN_POLISH (n open), or NEEDS_HUMAN (blocking or check problems left after the last attempt), and say which attempt was chosen.

issues.problem: Truth is judged only against the S1 material sheet, never the pack, so the reviewer cannot see what the pack marks as UNSOURCED or 'for visuals, not narration'. The final script states appearance and pose content as narration and gets truth 5. One line is also mis-cited: it lists a fact id that does not say what the line says.
issues.evidence: 'Look up. I'm still diving.' (no fact ids) comes from the pack's 'Pose (UNSOURCED) ... diving lunge' and 'Appearance (for visuals, not narration) ... suspended mid-dive'. 'Out there, I was blue, not bone.' cites juvenile_female, but the colour comes from the Appearance section. 06 thinking: 'The "still diving" line is a pose from the visual motif rather than a factual claim'. The reviewer wrote this line itself in 04.
issues.proposed_change: agent.s4_review: also pass `<knowledge_pack>{agent.pack(exhibit_id)}</knowledge_pack>`. Add to schemas.Review a field written first: `claims: list[Claim]` where Claim = {line: str, claim: str, fact_id: str, supported: bool}. Add to the s4 prompt, before the scores: "First, audit truth line by line. For every narration line, write each claim it makes about the exhibit or its history (including its colour, pose, size, age, sex, and what happened to it) and the one fact id that states it. A line that describes the exhibit's look or pose is still a claim. Visual motifs and anything the pack marks UNSOURCED or 'for visuals, not narration' are never support. If the cited fact does not itself say the claim, mark it unsupported, even when it is true. Any unsupported claim is a blocking issue and truth is 1." Add the same sentence about appearance and pose to the Narration paragraph of s3_script.md.

issues.problem: Self-grading and reviewer oscillation. The same model writes the replacement lines, then grades them. Its edits pull material from a rejected concept, and in the next round it criticises its own insertion. The S2 decision ('uses few facts') gets undone by the reviewer.
issues.evidence: In 04 the reviewer proposes 'Four and a half tonnes, just in bone.' (skeleton_weight, which is in concept 1, not in the chosen concept 0) and 'Look up. I'm still diving.' In 06 the same reviewer says the tonnage line 'pulls the film back to scale and blunts the surprise' and accepts its own diving line. Concept 0 fact_ids: length, juvenile_female, stranding_place, stranding_date, name_meaning.
issues.proposed_change: (1) Pass the chosen concept and the previous round's review to S4 from round 2 on. Add to the prompt: "Fixes must stay inside the chosen concept: use only its fact_ids unless a line is unsupported and needs a different fact. On round 2 and later, you get your previous review. Check each earlier issue (resolved / not resolved). Do not reverse a change you asked for unless it caused a new, named problem. Judge lines you suggested exactly as strictly as the writer's." (2) agent.py: let S4 use a different model through `HARNESS_REVIEW_MODEL` (for example claude-sonnet-5-5), and record it in meta. issues.problem: No per-line timing check. The budget is checked per segment only, so a line can run past the end of its segment, and in a 15 s Seedance generation it would be cut off or rushed. The final line also breaks the rule that the last ~1 s is for picture and sound.
issues.evidence: Final segment 2, line at 11.0 s: 'They named me Hope — for a future you can still shape.' is 11 words. At 2.5 w/s that is 4.4 s, so it ends at 15.4 s in a 15.0 s segment. Segment 1 line 2 (8 words at 3.4 s) runs to 6.6 s, past the next line at 6.4 s. All hard checks passed.
issues.proposed_change: In checks.script(), per segment: sort narration by t_start; for each line set `end = line.t_start + spoken_words(line.text) / WORDS_PER_SECOND`; flag if `end > next.t_start` ("line overlaps the next") or `end > seg.duration_s - 1.0` ("line runs into the last second / past segment end"); flag the first line if t_start < 0.8.

issues.problem: On-screen text is checked only in S3 shot fields, and only by a narrow regex. Concept hooks and endings are never checked, although a chosen concept carries straight into the script. The regex misses phrasings like 'figure "£250" fades in'.
issues.evidence: S2 concept 1 hook: 'Black screen, then a handwritten-style figure "£250" fades in over the shadow of her ribs.' checks.concepts() has no text test. TEXT_ON_SCREEN does not match 'fades in', 'handwritten', 'figure' or a quoted number. CHANGELOG v0 lists this too.
issues.proposed_change: Broaden the regex: `TEXT_ON_SCREEN = re.compile(r"\b(caption|title card|text|lettering|written|handwritten|typed|inscription|words?|numbers?|figures?|date|label|sign|logo|subtitle|on[- ]screen|fades? in|appears? on|superimposed)\b|[£$€]\s?\d|\"[^\"]*\d[^\"]*\"", re.I)`. Run it in checks.concepts() on hook and ending, and in checks.script() on visual, action and asset prompts minus any 'no text' phrase. For a clean signal, split Concept.hook in schemas.py into `hook_visual` (what is seen) and `hook_line` (what is heard), and run the text check on `hook_visual` only. Add to s2_concept.md: "The picture never contains text, numbers, dates, captions or titles; anything the visitor must read has to be spoken instead."

issues.problem: No code check ties the numbers in narration to the facts it cites. Mis-citations and derived numbers (arithmetic on two facts, which is not in the pack) get through. S1 fact texts are not checked against the pack either (only the source URL is).

issues.proposed_change: Add `numbers(text)`, which extracts digit groups and spelled numbers (one to ninety-nine, hundred, thousand, ordinals like 'twenty-fifth', with normalised 25.2 → 25 allowed as rounding). In checks.script(), flag any number in a line that appears in none of its cited facts' text, and any line with a number or capitalised place name but empty fact_ids. Run the same on concept hook_line and ending. In checks.material(), flag a fact whose numbers do not appear in pack_text.

issues.problem: Failures leave no trace. request.json is written before the call, but an exception (refusal, max_tokens, validation, network) writes nothing else, and run.py writes no report, so a crashed run looks like an empty folder. request_id is always null, so a bad call cannot be traced.

In _live_call, keep the raw text and write it to raw.txt before model_validate_json, so a schema failure can be inspected. Get the id with `stream.request_id` (or `response._request_id` from the non-stream client) and log it. best_things_to_keep: Each stage writes its own folder with request.json (full system prompt and user content, images redacted), thinking.md, output.json and meta.json (usage, cost, seconds, stop_reason, cached). That is exactly what made the 'rebuilding from scratch' and reviewer-oscillation problems visible.

The content-hash cache over {model, effort, prompt_file, system, user, schema}. Changing one prompt automatically invalidates that stage and everything downstream, while upstream stages stay frozen, which is the right base for fair A/B runs. Keep it and add a sample index.
Strict structured outputs built from pydantic (_strict_schema closes every object). Stage boundaries are typed, and the hard checks run on real fields, not on parsed prose.
Hard checks live in code (checks.py) and are fed both to the reviewer ('Automatic checks found') and to the writer as '[check]' feedback, so the loop cannot ignore a code-detected problem.

The knowledge-pack convention: a source per section, UNSOURCED sections, and 'Appearance (for visuals, not narration)'. Also checks.material() verifying each fact's source URL appears in the pack. The new sequoia and sophie packs already contain good traps.
Duration is decided in S1 and enforced in code (script duration must match the sheet; 1 or 2 segments; each segment at most 15 s; shot timecodes continuous).
S4's demand for concrete fixes with an exact location. Its round-1 notes were specific and actionable (the 'For your future' paraphrase drift, the triple 'young' repetition).
S2's three-concept-then-choose step with a written choice_reason, and S0's rule that a wrong match is worse than no match.
Prompts as separate files with a --variant mechanism, and CHANGELOG.md recording what a human saw on reading the output, not only scores.

report.md puts everything on the absolute film timeline (shot table, narration with fact ids, subtitles, assets), so a human can read the script quickly, which METHOD.md rightly treats as the main judgement.
